scope: Optional host-only backing-page write observer for single-core cache-corruption investigations. Not a guest hardware feature or performance/benchmark acceptance.
behavior: Compiled only with ir-test-hooks; absent from the production/fixed-core Wasm exports.
At most16 ordinary RAM pages; reject invalid slots, mapped I/O, out-of-range RAM and multiple cores.

Arm while stopped and invalidate cached translations. Existing checked code-dirty paths observe scalar, RMW, string, vector and host-device stores without page-table edits or injected guest exceptions. Keep observation when JIT code stops watching the same page.

4096 groups of24words: sequence, physical range, current/previous PC,CPL,CR3,eight registers,coalesced attempt count and32-byte page preimage. Adjacent stores at one PC/page/CR3 coalesce; future/expired ring reads reject.
NV_GUEST_WRITE_PAGES accepts hexadecimal physical page numbers. Host polling bounds stored records to65536 and reports overwritten/dropped groups. CPU sampling can run at the same time.

validation.writerForms: tests/x64/write_watch.asm/.mjs: scalar store,RMW XOR,REP MOVSD across pages,REP STOSD,unaligned SSE store across pages,XCHG; interpreter and compiled cases,watched/unwatched all produce identical8192-byte guest memory.
validation.ring: 40007 groups per watched case exercises wraparound and coalescing; reject expired/future records; explicit host DMA write observed and disarming stops observation.
validation.privilege: All16 tests/x64/legacy_wp_privilege.mjs cases with watch enabled retain exactly one user write #PF,error7,correctCR2 and unchanged legitimate kernel value; ordinary/PAE,small/large pages,read-before-write,interpreter/JIT.
validation.build: Release ir-test-hooks Wasm compiles; strict source/harness checks pass.

limits: Records occur before the underlying write and include a page prefix, not a whole-page postimage.
The observer can slow watched writes and therefore is for diagnosis, not native FPS measurements.
A matching writer PC still needs instruction/mapping analysis; no Win9803 root cause is claimed from adding the tool.
